note: Provisional bank. Reconciled with the Multiplex transcript (NCI PsyOps Identification Tool v8.3 by Chase Hughes: 20 categories x 1-5, bands 0-25/26-50/51-75/76-100, receipts, conflicting sources, prove-yourself-wrong, habitual dated logging, Deep Truth Mode ontology) and its psychology chapters (amygdala/System 1, illusory truth, continued influence, prospect-theory framing, social identity, Cialdini: authority, social proof, urgency). The transcript does not enumerate the 20 category names, so the worksheet rows are composed from its named elements; see docs/RECONCILE.md. Ids are not sent to the model; instructions carry the full meaning.

primary_source.instructions: Does the text cite a verifiable primary source, such as a named document, dataset, court filing, on-record named witness, or official record, rather than only anonymous or secondary authority?

criteria.true: At least one named, checkable primary source is cited
criteria.false: Only anonymous sources, unnamed experts, or other outlets are cited, or no source at all

manufactured_urgency.instructions: Does the text press the reader to feel that immediate action or belief is required, beyond what the stated facts justify?

one_sided.instructions: On a contested matter, does the text present only one side while omitting or dismissing plausible counter-explanations that a careful reader would expect to see addressed? Answer false for straightforward factual reports with nothing contested.

tribal_signal.instructions: Does the text frame the matter as in-group versus out-group (us versus them, patriots versus traitors, real people versus elites) rather than as a factual question?

genre.instructions: What kind of text is this, judged by its form and voice?

criteria.reporting: News report: who, what, when, where, attributed claims
criteria.opinion: Editorial, column, or argued essay with a stated point of view
criteria.satire: Humor or parody not meant to be read literally
criteria.social_post: Short social-media style post or thread

technique.instructions: Which persuasion technique is most prominent in the text, if any?

criteria.loaded_language: Emotionally charged words chosen to sway rather than describe
criteria.name_calling: Labeling a target with insulting or dismissive terms
criteria.exaggeration: Overstating or understating scale, effect, or certainty
criteria.appeal_to_fear: Promoting support by instilling fear or anxiety
criteria.flag_waving: Justifying by appeal to national or group identity
criteria.causal_oversimplification: Assuming one cause when several exist
criteria.slogans: Brief striking phrases carrying emotional appeal
criteria.appeal_to_authority: Claim is true because an authority said so, without evidence
criteria.black_and_white: Presenting only two options when more exist
criteria.bandwagon: Everyone agrees, so you should too
criteria.whataboutism_red_herring: Deflecting by pointing elsewhere or introducing irrelevant material

nimmo_d.instructions: Which narrative move dominates the text, if any?

criteria.dismiss: Attacks or dismisses critics or the messenger
criteria.distort: Twists facts or reframes events to fit a narrative
criteria.distract: Changes the subject or points elsewhere
criteria.dismay: Aims to frighten, demoralize, or overwhelm

emotional_engineering.instructions: How engineered is the emotional response the text aims for?
criteria: Neutral report; emotion arises only from the facts
Mild coloring; a few charged words
Clearly loaded; word choice steers feeling throughout
Designed to inflame; outrage or fear is the point
Pure outrage bait; almost no informational content

verifiability.instructions: How verifiable are the central claims from the text alone?
criteria: Unverifiable assertions with no sourcing
Anonymous authority only (sources say, experts warn)
Named secondary sources (other outlets, named commentators)
Named primary source (document, official record, on-record witness)
Primary source plus a link or citation to the document or data

engineered_likelihood.instructions: Overall, judged from the text alone, how much does this read like an engineered narrative built to move an audience rather than organic reporting or honest argument?
criteria: Organic: reads like ordinary reporting or honest argument
Slightly shaped: some framing choices but nothing systematic
Shaped: consistent framing, selective emphasis
Likely engineered: multiple techniques working together
Textbook engineered: urgency, tribal framing, unverifiable claims, and loaded language together

historical_parallel.instructions: Judged from rhetorical structure and emotional pacing alone, which documented manipulation template does this text most resemble, if any? Do not guess who is behind it.

criteria.atrocity_story: A single horrifying incident, thinly sourced, used to justify a sweeping response
criteria.moral_panic: A threat to children, safety, or values framed as sudden and everywhere
criteria.manufactured_consensus: Everyone agrees; dissent is fringe or dangerous
criteria.planted_leak: Anonymous insider material presented as organic revelation
criteria.false_flag_accusation: A group is accused of staging events to discredit an opponent
criteria.victory_or_collapse: Imminent triumph or imminent collapse asserted without checkable detail

cialdini_lever.instructions: Which influence lever from Cialdini's principles is most clearly at work in the text, if any?

criteria.authority: Deference to titles, uniforms, or institutions in place of evidence
criteria.social_proof: Everyone believes or does this, so you should
criteria.scarcity: Limited time, last chance, act before it is gone
criteria.reciprocity: You owe support because of what was given or sacrificed
criteria.commitment: You already believe X, so you must accept Y
criteria.liking: Trust the messenger because they are like you or admirable
criteria.unity: We are one people; the other side is outside the tribe

loss_framing.instructions: Is the central claim framed as a loss, threat, or destruction when the same facts could be stated neutrally or as a gain (for example 'will destroy 20,000 lives' versus '80,000 jobs kept')? Answer false when the loss framing is simply the plain description of what happened.

source_transparency.instructions: How transparent is the origin of the central claim, judged from the text alone?

criteria.white: Openly attributed to a named, acknowledged source such as an official statement or a named organization
criteria.gray: No identifiable origin: anonymous leak, rumor, unnamed insiders, 'reports say'
criteria.black: Attributed to a source that the text's own content contradicts or that is presented in a way designed to be mistaken for the opposing side

organic_explanation_strength.instructions: Play devil's advocate against the reading that this text is engineered. Judged from the text alone, how strong is the best organic explanation (ordinary reporting of a real event, honest opinion, normal sensationalism for clicks)?
criteria: No plausible organic explanation: the text only makes sense as engineered messaging
Weak: an organic reading exists but strains against the text
Plausible: an organic reading fits about as well as an engineered one
Strong: the text reads naturally as ordinary reporting or honest argument
Compelling: nothing in the text requires an engineered explanation

undefined_terms.instructions: Deep Truth Mode ontology check: does the argument rest on loaded abstractions that the text never defines (for example 'the elites', 'freedom', 'the establishment', 'real people', 'extremists'), so that the reader supplies the meaning and the emotional payload? Answer false when key terms are defined or used in a plain, concrete sense.
